title: Boipatong massacre
summary: On the night of 17 June 1992 an armed group, widely reported as Inkatha Freedom Party supporters from the nearby KwaMadala hostel, attacked residents of the Boipatong township in the Vaal Triangle, killing roughly 40 to 45 people. The ANC suspended constitutional talks, and responsibility, especially any police role, remained disputed.

uncertainty.note: Day given by the Commonwealth Oral History Project entry; the Mail & Guardian and O'Malley pages say only June 1992.

importance.justification: One of the deadliest episodes of political violence during the negotiated end of apartheid; it led the ANC to suspend talks.

audience_note: Describes a mass killing of civilians, including women and children, in a township. Death toll and the role of the police are disputed.

reviewer_note: Date 17 June is from one opened page (Commonwealth Oral History); the other opened pages give only June 1992. Death toll given as a range: about 40 (Commonwealth), more than 40 (Mail & Guardian), 45 (O'Malley page); the TRC figure of 46 was seen only in a search snippet and is not used. The police-involvement question is contested (TRC 1998 vs Amnesty Committee 2000). Pin is the township centre.
